name: community-cross-feeding
title: Cross-feeding in a two-species community
lead: This investigation demonstrates the CRM-FBA workspace end to end on its richest composite: two E. coli core models sharing one glucose/acetate pool, each a CRMProcess -> FBAStep pair. It asks whether the composite reproduces cross-feeding — the byproduct of one population becoming the niche of another.

at_a_glance.role: Runs the two-species community composite and shows the two offset growth phases + acetate overflow peak.

how_to_read: Open the two-species-community study: the biomass curves show the glucose specialist blooming first, the acetate pool peaking as glucose runs out, then the acetate specialist blooming on the byproduct.

glossary.definition: One population growing on a metabolic byproduct secreted by another.
Secretion of a partially-oxidized byproduct (here acetate) when uptake outpaces oxidative capacity.
Coexistence via use of different resources, rather than competition for one.

biological_story: Two E. coli populations share one flask of glucose and acetate. The glucose specialist takes up glucose fast but is oxygen-capped, so it spills acetate as overflow while it blooms and strips the glucose to zero. The acetate specialist barely moves during that first phase — but the flask is now full of acetate, exactly what it wants, and it blooms in a second phase on the byproduct. The offset between the two growth curves is the signature of cross-feeding: the metabolism of the first species creates the niche of the second, so they coexist instead of one excluding the other.
question: Can CRM-constrained dynamic FBA, composed as a multi-species bigraph on a shared nutrient pool, reproduce niche differentiation by cross-feeding rather than competitive exclusion?
hypothesis: A glucose specialist that overflows acetate under an O2 cap will build a byproduct pool that sustains a distinct acetate specialist, yielding two temporally offset growth phases.

executive.what_is_this: A one-study showcase of the CRM-FBA workspace's most impressive composite: a two-species E. coli community cross-feeding on a shared glucose/acetate pool.
executive.verdict: Confirmed — the composite reproduces cross-feeding: the glucose specialist blooms and overflows acetate, and the acetate specialist does 93% of its growth on that byproduct after the pool peaks.
executive.verdict_detail: glucose exhausted at t=8.3 coincident with a 17.4 mM acetate overflow peak; glucose specialist x116, acetate specialist x55 with 93% post-peak growth.

decisions_needed.question: Run the acetate-uptake-knockout negative control?
decisions_needed.context: The control that would isolate cross-feeding from competition is declared but not yet run.

scientific_argument.main_claim: The CRM-FBA composite reproduces cross-feeding-driven niche differentiation in a two-species community from only two Monod tunings, an O2 cap, and a shared FBA pool.
evidence_for: Glucose drawn to 0 by t=8.3 (glucose specialist x116).
Acetate overflow pool peaks at 17.4 mM, coincident with glucose exhaustion.
Acetate specialist grows x55 with 93% of growth after the acetate peak (temporal offset).
evidence_against: The acetate-uptake-knockout negative control that would exclude competition is not yet run.
caveats: Single well-mixed pool, no spatial structure.
Hand-tuned specialists, deterministic single run (no sweep yet).

studies.name: two-species-community
studies.title: Two-species cross-feeding community
studies.question: When a glucose specialist and an acetate specialist share a single glucose/acetate pool with no spatial separation, does CRM-constrained dynamic FBA reproduce niche differentiation by cross-feeding — i.e. does the glucose specialist's acetate overflow sustain distinct, temporally offset growth of the acetate specialist — rather than simple competitive exclusion?

resolved_uncertainties: The CRM-FBA composite can host a multi-species community on a shared pool and reproduce cross-feeding.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether cross-feeding survives an initial-biomass and O2-cap sweep.
Whether removing acetate uptake actually collapses the second growth phase (control pending).

followup_study_proposals.title: Negative control: knock out the acetate specialist's acetate uptake
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Directly isolate cross-feeding as the cause of the acetate specialist's post-peak growth by removing its ability to use the byproduct.

followup_study_proposals.title: Sweep the initial biomass split and O2 cap
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Establish the parameter regime over which the two-phase cross-feeding pattern holds versus collapses into competitive exclusion.

findings.statement: The glucose specialist blooms ~116x (0.008 -> 0.930 gDW) and drives the shared glucose pool to 0 by t=8.3.
Oxygen-capped glucose oxidation overflows acetate into the shared pool, which peaks at 17.4 mM at t=8.25 — coincident with glucose exhaustion.

evidence.observed: acetate pool peak 17.4 mM at t=8.25; glucose exhausted t=8.3

findings.statement: The acetate specialist grows ~55x, with 93% of its biomass gain occurring after the acetate peak — niche differentiation by cross-feeding, not competitive exclusion.

evidence.observed: acetate-specialist biomass x55; 7% pre-peak vs 93% post-peak growth

findings.next_action: Add a negative control that removes the acetate specialist's acetate uptake and confirm its growth collapses.

studies.claim: The glucose specialist's acetate overflow sustains a distinct acetate specialist: 93% of the acetate specialist's biomass gain occurs after the acetate pool peaks, and glucose is exhausted exactly at the peak (t=8.3) — niche differentiation by cross-feeding, not competitive exclusion.

biological_validation.basis: All three behaviours pass: glucose->0, acetate overflow peak (17.4 mM), and 93% post-peak acetate-specialist growth — the predicted cross-feeding signature.

regression_compatibility.basis: The crm_fba_community composite builds and runs 360 steps to completion with no solver errors; run persisted to runs.db.

explanatory_gain.basis: The community sorts into two temporally offset growth phases from only two Monod tunings + an O2 cap + a shared pool, distinguishing cross-feeding from competition (F-03).

derived.insight: The glucose specialist blooms ~116x (0.008 -> 0.930 gDW) and drives the shared glucose pool to 0 by t=8.3.
